title: [ORION-QG QG-32] Minimal separating probe basis above the bulk+spectrum abstraction lattice
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Direct parent: QG-31 #904 / committed query-indexed abstraction result.
ORION-Q transfer parent: MAX-R4E #903 / mechanism calibration #908.
Donor methods: minimum test cover / distinguishing set, set cover / hitting set, active feature acquisition, decision trees, experimental design, partition refinement.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE FRONTIER LANE. FREEZE BEFORE ANY MINIMUM-PROBE OUTCOME.**

QG-31 proves three exact observation partitions over the 715 TARE local-Clifford orbit types:
- bulk signature: 45 classes;
- unlabeled one-active defect spectrum: 54 classes;
- full indexed 384-probe response: 715 classes;
- bulk and spectrum are incomparable;
- even their joint information is not enough to recover the indexed response, because QG-31 has an explicit same-bulk + same-spectrum + different-indexed witness.

The next question is operational:

> Once the cheap bulk and unlabeled-spectrum summaries are known, what is the **smallest fixed subset of the 384 indexed probes** whose K-values make all 715 orbit types distinguishable?

No target cardinality is frozen. The answer may be large; a negative compression result is first-class.

## Q1 — exact joint base partition

Define

`A_joint(o) = (A_bulk(o), A_spectrum(o))`.

Reconstruct all 715 orbit types and report:
- exact number `N_joint` of joint classes;
- class-size histogram;
- all non-singleton class sizes;
- largest unresolved joint class;
- exact number of unresolved orbit pairs after joint summaries.

This count is a protected outcome, not a predeclared expectation.

## Q2 — fixed separating probe set

For probe index `p in {0,...,383}`, let `K_p(o)` be QG-31's ordered one-active response coordinate.

A probe subset `P` is **joint-separating** iff the map

`o -> (A_joint(o), (K_p(o))_{p in P})`

is injective on all 715 orbit types.

Find the minimum cardinality

`m_joint = min |P|`.

Required:
- explicit lexicographically canonical minimum probe set among all minima;
- for every selected probe: target permutation + auxiliary row + frame/Tag data;
- exact verification that all 715 signatures are distinct;
- lower-bound certificate showing no set of size `< m_joint` separates all unresolved pairs.

## Q3 — exact hitting-set formulation

Build the unresolved-pair universe only within joint classes. For every probe `p`, define the set of unresolved pairs it distinguishes.

A valid probe basis is exactly a hitting/set-cover solution over these pair constraints.

The production solver may use branch-and-bound, ILP, SAT, or exhaustive combinatorial search, but the committed result must include a solver-independent certificate that the generic verifier can reconstruct:
- unresolved-pair count;
- selected probe set;
- coverage witness for every pair;
- lower-bound proof object appropriate to the solver (e.g. disjoint/private pair packing, exact branch certificate, or independently replayable exhaustive layer failure).

A heuristic set without a minimum proof earns only `UPPER_BOUND` authority.

## Q4 — baselines / ablations

Also report, without conflating their authority:

1. `m_raw` or best exact bounds for probes needed if **no** bulk/spectrum summary is supplied;
2. probes needed above **bulk only**;
3. probes needed above **spectrum only**;
4. probes needed above **joint bulk+spectrum**.

If exact minima for all four are computationally expensive, QG-32's primary theorem is `m_joint`; the others may be certified bounds.

This ablation measures the value of combining cheap summary observations before active probing.

## Q5 — adaptive successor registration

A fixed probe basis may still be wasteful. If `m_joint` is nontrivial, register but do not silently execute a successor for an adaptive decision tree minimizing:
- worst-case number of probes;
- mean probes under frozen orbit priors;
- or both.

Do not call the fixed-basis result an adaptive optimum.

## Q6 — ORION-Q interpretation

If a small exact `m_joint` is earned, the allowed ORION-Q research-control statement is:

> For this compiler-local observation problem, cheap bulk+spectrum summaries plus `m_joint` fixed indexed probes recover the complete 715-way local-response identity, so a finer claim can be authorized by active acquisition rather than carrying all 384 indexed responses by default.

This is a domain-specific active-verification primitive. It does not establish generic optimal experimental design.

If `m_joint` is large, that is equally useful: it quantifies the information barrier and tells ORION-Q not to expect cheap active recovery.

## Independent verification

Production:
- binds QG-31 committed receipt;
- reconstructs exact 715×384 response matrix;
- solves the minimum joint-separating probe problem.

Generic ORION:
- independently rebuilds phase-free F2^2/F3 semantics, 715 local-Clifford orbits, 384 probes, joint partition and pair-distinguishing matrix;
- verifies the selected set and minimum proof without importing the production solver.

Native ORION-Q:
- authorizes only the fixed-probe, query-scoped active-verification result;
- no global optimizer/minimal-state/physical authority.

## Claim ladder

- `QG32_JOINT_PARTITION_RECONSTRUCTED`
- `QG32_JOINT_SEPARATING_PROBE_UPPER_BOUND_CERTIFIED`
- `QG32_MINIMUM_JOINT_SEPARATING_PROBE_BASIS_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- successor only: adaptive probe tree optimality.

## Hard boundaries

Mandatory false unless separately proved:
- minimum probes for the full finite-n optimum;
- minimum experimental measurements on hardware;
- global QG-28 state minimality;
- generic active-learning/test-cover novelty;
- physical quantum advantage.

## Intended strong terminal

`QG32_MINIMUM_FIXED_PROBE_BASIS_ABOVE_JOINT_BULK_SPECTRUM_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Honest alternatives: only an upper/lower bound, joint response unexpectedly injective (contradicts parent and should fail parent binding), solver certificate gap, generic/native disagreement, or CANNOT_CHECK.
